big_picture_notes: Titus is a pastoral letter in standard Hellenistic epistolary form: salutation (1:1–4), main didactic body (1:5–3:11), and conclusion (3:12–15). The core movement interweaves practical ethics with dense theological summaries, producing a chiastic feel: false teachers → household/communal ethics → grace/renewal rationale → civic conduct → warning against factious persons. Literary glue includes ‘sound doctrine’ vs false teaching, frequent ‘for/gar’ rationales, and the repeated emphasis on ‘good works’ as the fruit of God’s saving action (2:14; 3:1, 8, 14).

stories.story_title: The Commission and the Conflict in Crete
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (1:1) epistolary salutation opens; end (1:16) closes with the summary verdict on the opponents (‘they profess… deny by works’). Glue: commission→conflict motif linking Paul’s authority (1:1–4) to Titus’s task (1:5), bridged by elder qualifications (1:6–9) as antidote to false teachers (1:10–16).

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Paul, servant and apostle for the faith and hope of eternal life, greets Titus his true child.

scenes.scene_name: The Task and the Elder's Character
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Why Titus was left in Crete: appoint blameless elders who hold firmly to sound teaching.
Many empty deceivers who upset households for gain — even a Cretan prophet condemned them.

scenes.scene_name: Rebuke Them Sharply; They Deny God by Their Deeds
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A stern rebuke for the defiled who profess to know God but are unfit for any good work.

stories.story_title: The Pattern of Sound Doctrine and Good Works
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (2:1) ‘But you—teach what accords with sound doctrine’ shifts to positive instruction; end (3:11) definitive handling of the divisive person. Glue: repeated ‘good works’ motif and didactic flow: household ethics → grace epiphany rationale → civic virtues → insistence and warning.

scenes.scene_name: Sound Doctrine for Older Men and Women
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Titus to teach the older men temperance and the older women reverence as teachers of good.

scenes.scene_name: Train the Young Women and Young Men
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The older women training the young in love and self-control; the young men urged to self-control.

scenes.scene_name: Be a Model of Good Works
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Titus himself an example of integrity and wholesome speech, leaving opponents nothing to fault.

scenes.scene_name: Slaves Adorning the Doctrine of God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Submissive, honest servants who make the teaching about God our Savior attractive.
Saving grace trains us to await the blessed hope of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.

scenes.scene_name: Submit to Authorities; We Too Were Once Foolish
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Be peaceable and ready for good work, remembering our own former enslavement to passions.

scenes.scene_name: Saved by Mercy Through the Washing of Rebirth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Not by works but by His mercy and the renewing Spirit, justified as heirs of eternal life.

scenes.scene_name: Insist on Good Works; Reject the Divisive
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Devote to good deeds, avoid pointless controversies, and reject a divisive man after two warnings.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (3:12) travel logistics and personal plans signal the close; end (3:15) final grace benediction. Glue: named coworkers, travel/greeting notes, and a last nudge toward good works in practical support.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Come to Nicopolis, equip Zenas and Apollos, learn good works — and grace be with all.
